topSignals.title: New York's data center moratorium contains a self-generation clause — direct SOFC regulatory tailwind
topSignals.text: — Governor Hochul's Executive Order No. 62 (signed July 14, 2026) imposes a one-year hyperscale moratorium on new data centers ≥50 MW pending a Generic Environmental Impact Statement, but the embedded "Energize NY" proceeding is the strategically critical element: the Department of Public Service is directed to require data centers to either (a) self-supply their electricity or (b) pay higher rates to avoid shifting grid upgrade costs onto residential ratepayers. This is the first US state-level regulatory trigger mandating on-site generation as the preferred data center power model. If Energize NY yields rules that price grid power at a significant premium over self-supply for data centers, SOFC becomes the default qualifying technology — continuous, dispatchable, gas-fueled, installable in 90 days. New York is the third-largest US data center market after Northern Virginia and Silicon Valley. NY Governor EO No. 62 | CNBC | Washington Post

topSignals.title: FERC generation adequacy reports due tomorrow (July 20) — first public quantification of firm-power gap by region
topSignals.text: — All six RTOs/ISOs (PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE) must file informational reports by July 20 detailing how adequate generation will serve new large loads (≥50 MW, ≥69 kV), with stakeholder proposals, milestone schedules, and ongoing proceedings. This is the first mandated public disclosure of the region-by-region firm-power shortfall that is driving the SOFC grid-bypass market. Monday's filings will be the primary sizing input for SOFC addressable market by geography: any region projecting a >5-year queue backlog with no credible near-term supply addition is, in effect, a validated SOFC market. Mark as an immediate model-input trigger. FERC RM26-4 | Utility Dive | McGuireWoods

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy at $216, -38.5% from ATH — 247wallst frames "growth story starting to crack" as earnings countdown begins
topSignals.text: — A July 18 247wallst analysis synthesizes the accumulated execution-risk signals: Project Jupiter's second pipeline denial, New York's data center moratorium, and broadening community resistance to data center construction are together eroding the "infinite addressable market" narrative that drove the $351 ATH. BE closed July 18 at approximately $216 (intraday $194.60–$223.75), +149% YTD but -38.5% from peak. Markets are closed today (Sunday July 19). Q2 earnings on July 28 (AH) — now 9 days away — remain the sole reset event: consensus calls for ~$804M revenue, $0.36 EPS, ~34% gross margin. The gap between disclosed deal flow ($20B backlog, $25B Brookfield, $1.7B Oaktree/IDF project finance) and current market cap implies the market is now pricing project delivery timing rather than deal announcements. 247wallst — "starting to crack" | stockinvest.us

Elcogen (E3000 G2: ≥75% electrical / ≥90% CHP at 650°C), Ceres licensees (Doosan yield trajectory), SolydEra, and Convion have published nothing online since the conference. One EFCF paper has appeared in the publicly accessible archive (large-stack EIS study, EFCF 2026) but no product-level efficiency or durability results from the major developers. Monitor elcogen.com, ceres.tech, solydera.com, convion.fi.

Energy Transfer's 30-day administrative review window runs to approximately August 13; October 19 air permit hearing (NMED decision by November 23) remains the gating event. Weekend — no new filings or announcements.

Active pipeline unchanged: Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1 (H2 2026), FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW, AEP/Bloom 1 GW (Wyoming, 2030), Bloom/Brookfield $25B EaaS, Nebius 328 MW EaaS ($1.7B Oaktree/IDF project finance closed July 16).

New York data center moratorium (EO No. 62, July 14) — See Top Signal #1. Full detail: one-year pause on DEC permits for new hyperscale data centers ≥50 MW. GEIS process will assess electricity demand, grid impact, water, and air quality. "Energize NY" DPS proceeding (parallel to GEIS) will set rules requiring data centers to self-generate or pay surcharges. The moratorium exempts permits already deemed complete and does not block projects already under construction. For SOFC market development in New York: no new data center projects in queue means no new SOFC deployments in NY for 12 months minimum, but the Energize NY self-supply rules — when finalized — could make New York the most SOFC-favorable regulatory environment in the US for large data centers post-moratorium. Governor NY press release | NBC News | Fox Business

FERC RM26-4 reports due July 20 — See Top Signal #2. ISO-NE 90-day abeyance request (if granted) pushes its filing to approximately August 3; full tariff reform or show-cause justifications due August 17. All other five RTOs/ISOs are expected to file Monday.

Background unchanged: Virginia DC electricity tax $0.011/kWh (self-generated SOFC not exempt, July 1); Germany EnEfG amendment (cabinet adoption June 24, Bundestag/Bundesrat approval pending); EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed into Q3; Section 179D sunset confirmed June 30; ITC 48E 30% fuel cell credit active.

Terrestrial Energy + Riot Platforms: 4 GW IMSR nuclear for Texas/Kentucky data centers (first appearance) — Announced May 6, 2026 (not captured in prior digests). MOU to co-locate Terrestrial Energy's Integral Molten Salt Reactor (IMSR, 390 MW per unit) plants with Riot Platforms data centers. Up to 4 GW total across multiple sites (primary candidates: Riot's Rockdale, TX and Paducah, KY facilities). First commercial IMSR plants targeted for early 2030s. Natural gas bridge fuel included to accelerate commercial start. Context: this is a ~6-8 year horizon project — not a near-term SOFC competitor. But the IMSR's 390 MW module size and potential for co-location with existing data center sites more directly competes with the SOFC model than conventional AP1000 nuclear (1.1 GW, greenfield only). Riot Platforms PR | BusinessWire | Minichart Q1 results context

lcoe.text: New York Energize NY self-supply premium — new regulatory LCOE variable — If the DPS proceeding creates a grid-supply surcharge for large data centers, it establishes a state-mandated floor price for grid power that makes the SOFC self-supply option economically rational even before capacity or speed arguments. The exact surcharge level is unknown (GEIS + rulemaking will take up to 12 months), but analogous mechanisms in other jurisdictions (Germany's EEG surcharge structure, Virginia's DC-specific tariff) suggest a $10–30/MWh premium is plausible. Add as a "regulatory upside" sensitivity in the LCOE model for any New York project: SOFC LCOE advantage = avoided grid surcharge + avoided transmission charges. This could bring SOFC to economic parity with grid supply in NY before ITC 48E.

FERC reports July 20 — extract firm-power gap by RTO/ISO — Tomorrow's filings will provide the first regulator-mandated public estimate of the generation shortfall serving new large loads in each US grid region. Key metric to extract: total confirmed large-load MW seeking grid connection that cannot be served within 5 years per region. This sets the de facto ceiling of the SOFC grid-bypass addressable market. Immediate update trigger upon filing.

BE intraday range July 18 ($194.60–$223.75): the $194.60 intraday low implies the market tested — and rejected — the below-$200 level. The recovery to $216 at close suggests buy-side support remains at current levels ahead of the July 28 print. Not a fundamental input but relevant context for interpreting post-Q2 market signals on execution risk repricing.

Terrestrial Energy IMSR: 390 MW module — At $4,000–6,000/kW nuclear capex (pre-cost reduction) and 2030+ delivery, IMSR does not change near-term SOFC LCOE competition; but at commercial scale its 390 MW modular size could compete directly with SOFC aggregated projects in the 2032+ window. Flag as a long-run (>2030) downside scenario in multi-decade LCOE model.
